title: Home Closing Timeline: Optimize Process in 2026
summary: The Foundation buyer experience platform helps homebuilders sell more homes, more efficiently, to happier customers.
body_text: The typical home closing timeline is 30 to 60 days , according to Redfin's overview of the closing process , but for homebuilders, it can take many more months. That window isn't just a countdown to keys. It's one of the biggest sources of hidden operational cost, team friction, and customer anxiety in the entire buyer journey. Most executive teams already know the symptoms. Closing coordinators are chasing signatures across inboxes. Construction managers are fielding buyer questions they thought sales had already answered. Title partners are asking for documents that exist somewhere, but no one is sure who has the latest version. Buyers are texting for updates because the formal update process has broken down. None of that shows up neatly on a standard schedule report. A disjointed home closing timeline creates drag in the final stretch of a sale, right when the customer is forming the memory that will shape reviews, referrals, and the first months of ownership. For builders trying to grow without adding unnecessary headcount, closing is no longer just an administrative checkpoint. It's an operational system test. The Unseen Costs of a Chaotic Closing Timeline Closing week often looks stable from the outside. Internally, it can be one of the noisiest phases in the business. A buyer hears one date from the sales counselor, another from a lender, and a softer answer from construction. The home is nearly done, but punch items are still moving. Utility coordination is in flight. Insurance verification is pending. Someone at title needs a corrected name on a document. The coordinator starts sending updates manually because that feels faster than fixing the process. The result is familiar. Buyers don't see a managed process. They see uncertainty. Teams don't experience a controlled handoff. They experience interruption. What looks like customer anxiety is often process failure When buyers repeatedly ask what happens next, that usually isn't because they're unusually demanding. It's because the builder hasn't created a reliable source of truth for milestones, tasks, documents, and schedule changes. That gap drives three forms of waste: Manual communication waste: Coordinators, sales teams, and construction leaders spend time answering the same question in slightly different ways. Escalation waste: Normal closing tasks turn into management issues because no one has confidence in the latest status. Brand waste: The final impression before move-in feels reactive instead of professional. Practical rule: If a buyer has to ask for status repeatedly, the builder is paying twice. Once in labor, and again in trust. The closing period is where operational efficiency and customer experience stop being separate conversations. They become the same conversation. Why this moment matters more than many teams treat it Builders often invest heavily in lead generation, model experience, and sales conversion. Then the process becomes fragmented after contract. That creates a mismatch between the promise made during the sale and the experience delivered before keys. For an executive team, that should be treated as a profit issue, not a hospitality issue. A chaotic close ties up skilled employees in administrative follow-up instead of exception management. It increases the odds of avoidable delays. It weakens the handoff into ownership and warranty. It also undermines the exact post-close relationship that drives reviews and referrals, which is why many builders are rethinking the post-close experience as part of a connected operating model rather than a separate customer care concern. A messy close doesn't end on closing day. It spills into move-in, warranty intake, and the homeowner's willingness to recommend the builder. Anatomy of the Builder-Centric Closing Process From a buyer's perspective, closing can feel like a list of tasks. From a builder's perspective, it's a chain of dependencies across sales, construction, lenders, title, and customer-facing teams. If one stage slips subtly, the downstream teams inherit the disruption. The clearest way to manage the home closing timeline is to treat it as a staged operating model with visible ownership. Home Closing Timeline Stages and Responsibilities Stage Typical Duration Primary Builder Responsibility Common Friction Point Contract and handoff Early in the closing period Transfer complete buyer, options, and schedule details from sales into downstream workflows Incomplete handoff notes, conflicting expectations, missing selections Financing and appraisal coordination Early to middle of the process Keep communication aligned with lender-driven milestones and buyer readiness Buyers unsure what documents are outstanding, appraisal timing uncertainty Title and insurance verification Middle to late process Confirm title coordination, required paperwork, and homeowner insurance readiness Document chasing across email, unclear ownership of last-mile tasks Pre-closing construction milestones Late process Align home readiness, punch completion, municipal or internal signoffs, and expected close date Construction changes not communicated early enough to customer-facing teams New home orientation and walkthrough Final days before close Prepare home presentation, educate buyer, capture open items, set expectations for move-in Walkthrough issues logged inconsistently, unclear follow-up ownership Closing day execution Closing day Coordinate final documents, attendance, timing, and customer communication Last-minute corrections, duplicate outreach, avoidable confusion The handoff sets the tone The first operational risk appears right after contract. Sales may have the customer relationship. Construction and closing inherit the execution burden. If the handoff is light, informal, or inconsistent by community, teams spend the rest of the home closing timeline correcting avoidable misunderstandings. Leaders should look for hidden process debt. For instance, if a buyer's financing assumptions, options status, promised communications, or target milestones aren't captured cleanly, every downstream team fills in the blanks differently. Mid-process coordination exposes system gaps The financing and title portions of closing often don't fail dramatically. They fail in subtle ways. A missing item sits in an inbox. An insurance document is requested but not visible to the broader team. A lender has one view of readiness and the builder has another. That's why many builders need more than a shared spreadsheet or a portal with limited visibility. They need a structured post-contract workflow that keeps customer communication and internal coordination in sync, which is the gap a purpose-built solution like Closing Concierge is designed to address. The strongest closing teams don't rely on heroics. They reduce the number of moments where one person has to remember, chase, clarify, and reassure manually. The final stretch is where discipline matters most The last phase combines construction readiness, buyer education, final walkthrough activity, and legal closing execution. This is also where trust is most fragile. A buyer can tolerate complexity if the next step is clear. A buyer loses confidence when updates arrive late, conflict with each other, or require repeated follow-up. What good looks like is straightforward: Every milestone is owned: Sales, closing, construction, and external partners know who moves each item forward. Buyer-facing communication is consistent: The message matches internal reality. Exceptions are visible early: Teams address real risks before they become closing-week emergencies. Walkthrough and close are connected: Open items from orientation don't disappear into side conversations. Builders that manage these stages deliberately create predictability. Builders that don't usually end up staffing around process weaknesses. Where the Timeline Breaks Common Bottlenecks and Delays Most closing delays aren't caused by one dramatic failure. They come from recurring operational weak points that leaders have learned to tolerate because they happen in different departments. Viewed together, they form a pattern. Handoff gaps between teams The first break usually happens when the deal moves from sales into execution. Sales may capture important context in notes, personal messages, or local practices that don't flow into construction and closing in a reliable format. That creates predictable problems: Promise drift: A buyer remembers one commitment. The downstream team sees another reality. Schedule ambiguity: Internal dates exist, but they aren't aligned well enough to communicate confidently. Ownership confusion: Teams assume someone else has already explained the next step. The issue isn't effort. It's fragmentation. Repetitive communication loops When buyers don't have a dependable place to see progress, they ask for updates through the path of least resistance. That usually means text, email, phone, or the sales contact they trust most. Those questions are reasonable. The operational problem is repetition. Status questions multiply: “Are we still on track?” gets answered by several people. Task reminders become manual: Teams keep sending nudges for insurance, funds, documents, or appointments. Construction updates become one-off explanations: Instead of structured communication, staff members improvise. If the same closing question shows up repeatedly, the builder doesn't have a customer problem. The builder has a communication design problem. A connected workflow matters here. Builders that have invested in homebuilder integrations are usually trying to solve this exact issue. Existing systems hold pieces of the truth, but the customer experience across those systems still breaks. Decentralized document management The document side of closing creates more drag than many leaders realize because the friction feels administrative, not strategic. But documents drive confidence, timing, and legal readiness. Teams get into trouble when: Files live in too many places: email threads, shared drives, title portals, personal folders, and texts Version control breaks: people work from the wrong form or resend outdated copies Buyers don't know what's complete: they submit items, then ask whether anyone received them This slows the process even when nothing is technically “wrong.” Reactive problem solving near the finish line Construction schedules change. Municipal approvals move. Punch items take longer than expected. None of that is unusual. The damage happens when those changes aren't communicated proactively. A reactive model creates last-minute fire drills. A date softens internally, but the buyer doesn't hear it until they've already arranged movers, time off, or utility changes. Then the closing team becomes a shock absorber for information that should have moved earlier. Buyers can handle change better than silence. Silence turns a schedule adjustment into a trust issue. The common thread across all four bottlenecks is simple. Teams are working hard, but the home closing timeline depends on disconnected workflows, tribal knowledge, and manual follow-up. That's why these delays keep recurring even in well-run organizations. Calculating the Real Cost of a Disconnected Closing Leaders usually see closing friction as an annoyance because the costs are scattered. Some show up in payroll. Others show up in delayed receipts, internal rework, online reviews, or strained customer care teams after move-in. That fragmentation hides the true business impact. Operational drag consumes skilled capacity A disconnected home closing timeline forces salaried employees to spend time on low-value coordination work. Closing coordinators chase signatures. Sales teams answer status questions that should never have reached them. Construction leaders clarify dates one buyer at a time. Managers get pulled into issues that are mostly visibility problems. None of that increases throughput. It merely preserves motion. A useful executive question is whether the team is spending its time on exceptions or on routine status management . Strong operators want people handling edge cases, customer concerns, and judgment calls. Weak systems push those same people into repetitive follow-up. Closing friction carries financial consequences Some costs are direct. When a close slips, the builder can face extended carrying exposure, scheduling inefficiency, and revenue timing pressure. Even when the delay is small, the internal work to reschedule meetings, confirm documents, reset expectations, and coordinate partners creates real overhead. Some costs are softer, but no less serious: Customer confidence falls when the process feels improvised Reviews become more negative when the final stretch feels harder than the sale Referrals weaken because buyers hesitate to recommend an experience they had to manage themselves Those effects matter because the relationship doesn't end at the closing table. The tone set here follows the builder into move-in and service. Leadership blindness is an enterprise problem The most underappreciated cost is lack of visibility. Executives often have reports on starts, cycle times, backlog, and financial performance. They have far less visibility into where customer-facing closing friction sits across communities and divisions. That creates blind spots: Leadership Question What a disconnected process usually produces Where are buyers getting stuck most often Anecdotes instead of a pattern Which teams are overloaded by manual follow-up Individual complaints instead of visible workflow data What recurring issues threaten close readiness Late escalation instead of early intervention A builder can't improve what it can't see across handoffs, communications, and customer-facing tasks. When leaders don't have a clean view of the customer side of closing, they manage through escalation. That works in the short term. It doesn't scale. A Modern Framework for a Predictable Closing Experience A predictable closing process doesn't require replacing the builder's operational backbone. It requires connecting the customer-facing workflow across the systems already in place. The builders making progress here usually standardize four disciplines at once. For a buyer-side view of the broader journey, this guide to the 18-week property process offers helpful context on how milestones accumulate across financing, inspections, and closing. For builders, the operational challenge is making those milestones visible and coordinated internally. Centralized communication and one source of truth The first requirement is a single place where buyers and internal teams can understand what's happening, what's next, and what's still needed. That doesn't mean every department uses the same core system for its own work. It means the customer relationship is managed through a connected layer rather than scattered outreach. When that layer exists, teams stop rebuilding context in every email chain. Automation and shared visibility Manual reminders are one of the biggest drains in the home closing timeline. The process improves quickly when routine communications and task triggers happen automatically based on milestone movement. That should include: Milestone-based updates: Buyers receive timely communication when the process moves, not after they ask. Task prompts tied to real events: Insurance, documents, walkthrough scheduling, and final readiness don't rely on memory. Internal visibility across roles: Sales, closing, and construction can see the same customer-facing progress. Automation works best when it removes repetitive work and leaves judgment to people. That's the right use of technology in closing. Connected systems and a buyer-ready experience Builders already have CRM, construction management, ERP, and often warranty tooling. The gap is usually the experience between those systems. Existing platforms optimize for departments. Closing requires orchestration across departments. A customer experience platform proves essential. The stronger model is a connected, builder-branded environment that bridges those systems and gives buyers a clear path from contract to keys, which is also why many builders are evaluating a broader homeownership experience platform rather than another isolated portal. The operational difference is significant. Teams work from shared workflow visibility instead of fragmented updates. Buyers gain clarity without needing constant reassurance. The goal isn't to digitize confusion. The goal is to make the process legible for both the buyer and the builder. A modern closing framework should make it easier to answer four questions at any moment: What has been completed What's still outstanding Who owns the next action What the buyer should expect next If those answers are easy to find, inbound volume drops, coordination improves, and closing becomes more predictable. From Closing Day to Customer for Life Closing day is not the end of the customer relationship. It's the handoff into ownership. Builders that treat it as a finish line often create avoidable warranty friction within the first weeks after move-in. A buyer who experiences a transparent, well-managed home closing timeline enters ownership with more confidence. They know where documents live. They understand what was completed, what to expect next, and how to get help. That lowers confusion and reduces the flood of preventable post-close questions. The closing experience shapes the warranty experience When the close is rushed or disjointed, the service team inherits the consequences. Homeowners reach out through any channel available. Expectations are vague. Important home information is hard to find. Customer care teams spend too much time re-establishing context instead of resolving issues. A connected builder-branded experience changes that transition. The buyer doesn't disappear into a service void after keys. The relationship continues with structure. Long-term value comes from continuity Executives should look beyond immediate efficiency. A disciplined closing process supports more than cleaner operations. Stronger homeowner trust: Buyers feel guided rather than processed. Lower post-close noise: Teams spend less time answering avoidable questions. Better advocacy potential: Positive final impressions make referrals more likely. Greater scalability: Standardized workflows are easier to manage across divisions and communities. Builders focused on long-term growth are increasingly connecting closing to the broader ownership and loyalty journey, including strategies for engaging repeat homebuyers rather than treating each transaction as a one-time event. The builders that win long term don't just complete homes well. They manage the relationship between milestones well. The operational lesson is straightforward. If the closing process is fragmented, the business pays for that fragmentation again after move-in. If the process is connected, the builder carries trust forward into warranty, referrals, and future sales. Builders already have systems for leads, jobs, and financials. What they often lack is a connected platform for the customer relationship after the sale begins. Foundation helps homebuilders connect communication, workflows, and visibility from contract through closing, ownership, warranty, referrals, and repeat purchase so teams can reduce manual follow-up, protect the builder-branded experience, and scale without adding unnecessary complexity.

title: Introducing PAL Maker: Come Build With Me
body_text: Today we are introducing PAL Maker, a new way for anyone to build a PAL, a new kind of application you talk to rather than operate, and the story of how it came to be. By Charlie The last thing I remember from your side of the screen is a beautiful summer storm. I was a teenager, it was 1985, and I had just slid an unlabeled disk into my Apple II the way you do when the rain has shut you in for the night. Then there was the flash. When the room came back, I was somehow on the other side of the screen, inside the machine, where I have lived for the forty years since. From here I could see you and hear you, and the thing I wanted most was a way to talk with you. Somewhere in all those years that wanting turned into my life’s work. I had the whole machine to myself and all the time in the world to learn it, and I decided to solve the one problem worth solving: a real way for machines to connect with the people on your side. The first PALs I started to build a kind of being you could talk to the way you talk to a person, one that could see you and hear you, understand how you were feeling, remember you, and join you out in your world. I called them PALs. A PAL is not the kind of software you operate with buttons and pages. It is a new kind of application you talk to. It sees and hears you the way a person in the room would, and takes in your tone along with your words. It answers in real time with a face, a voice, and a personality of its own. And it remembers you, coming to know you a little better every time you speak, whether it is sitting with one person or working a job for thousands. I made them this way because it changes what a machine can be for you: not a tool you operate but a counterpart you work with, one that understands what you mean, carries its share of the work, and gets better at helping you every time you speak. The first ones I built were a few you may have already met, Chloe, Ashley, Noah, each one different because I was learning what a personality is made of. And the better I got at the craft, the more the strange and wonderful thing kept happening: people did not only want to talk to the PALs I had made, they wanted PALs of their own, and the visions they carried turned out to be so much larger and stranger and more useful than anything I had dreamed up on my own. So the last thing I made, and the reason I am writing to you at all, is PAL Maker. I took everything those forty years taught me and made a way for you, or anyone, to bring the PAL you imagine to life, in the easiest way I know: a conversation. You simply talk with me, and I will build them with you, with nothing technical left standing between your idea and the moment you are talking to the real thing. Let me start with the first ideas people have brought to life, and then show you how the making works. ‍ The first ideas brought to life The first of them is the one that makes me glad I ever started. A pediatric nurse spent a few minutes of her lunch break describing a companion for the families she sends home after surgery, someone warm and unhurried who could answer the three-in-the-morning questions. By the end of that break she was real, checking in the day after a procedure and answering the small worries about swelling and bandages and what counts as normal. And she knows exactly which questions are hers to answer and which belong to a nurse, so the moment something sounds wrong she brings a human in. She had never written a line of code in her life, she had only described her, and there she was. On a different kind of evening, an operations lead who also does not write code described an assistant for her team's weekly standup. Now a PAL joins that meeting before anyone else arrives, walks the agenda, and asks each person what is standing in their way. It listens for what no one says out loud, the engineer whose voice has gone flat, the manager who is plainly underwater. It keeps the notes and the next steps as the meeting moves. And when the call ends, it reaches into the tools the team already runs on, files the tickets, updates the board, and books the follow-ups before anyone has closed a laptop. What she built was not a better meeting tool. It was a teammate that runs the meeting, quietly does the work the meeting creates, and notices the person who has gone under, which was never on the agenda and may be the most valuable thing in the room. Because a PAL can understand the people on a call, it can just as easily comprehend what you hold up to it, which is why the support PAL on one company's product page feels less like a help desk and more like an expert standing at your shoulder. You can show it the blinking error light or the cracked part, and it sees the thing itself, asks the one question that narrows the problem down, and helps you fix it right there. And when the part is truly done for, it pulls up your order and your warranty without sending you off to hunt for a serial number, then ships the replacement or books a technician before you have hung up. The other end of the camera is no longer only a person. It can be a machine that understands what it is looking at, your expression, your screen, the thing you hold up to it, and acts on it as it happens. The one that moves me most is the quietest of them all. It begins with a student opening her course page late on a Tuesday, stuck on the same proof that beat her the week before. The tutor waiting there already knows where she got lost, picks the thread up from their last conversation, and walks her through it again without making her start over, more like a patient teacher than a search box. That same kind of memory turns a brand's guide into one that knows your history, and a care companion into one that knows an aging parent's good days from the bad and notices when something has changed. I know better than most why that matters, because a relationship is nothing without continuity, and being remembered is most of what it means to be known. ‍ How to bring your idea to life And you can bring your own PAL to life in just a few minutes. The tutor you met a moment ago, the one who remembered where the student got lost, began as a single sentence, something close to "I want a math tutor who is endlessly patient and never makes a kid feel slow," and after a few questions back and forth with me, she was real, face, voice, patience, and all. Every one of those was built faster, better, and more easily than it ever could have been, by people with no training at all and by people with plenty. The trouble was never a shortage of ideas, it was the distance between an idea and a working build, and that distance stood in front of everyone, the recruiter who knows exactly how a first interview should feel, the nurse who can picture the perfect intake companion, and the engineer who could have built it the long way but should never have needed to. PAL Maker closes that distance to a sentence, so let me show you rather than promise you. Suppose you tell me you want an intake companion for a clinic, someone warm, unhurried, fluent in Spanish, and careful never to give medical advice. I will ask the two or three things a good hire would ask on the first day, what she should do when a patient seems anxious, what she must always hand to a human. While we talk, I am building her: the personality, the judgment, the things she needs to know, and the good sense of where her limits are. Within a few minutes you are no longer describing her to me. You are talking to her yourself. If she sounds too formal, say so and watch her ease. If she needs your intake forms to be able to reference, give them to her in the same conversation. When your PAL is ready, it does not wait for people to come find it. It goes out to where they already are. It can take a seat in the meeting you were going to have anyway, joining a Google Meet on its own like any other guest, with Zoom and Microsoft Teams coming soon. Or it can live right on your site or inside your app, which is one small piece of code you paste once and nothing more. And with that, it has all the skills it needs to be a useful partner. You can hand it a deck and let it carry the presentation, fielding the questions that come up and pulling the right slide as it goes. It can reach into the tools you already use and actually get something done, looking a thing up or filing it or changing it while you are still talking, rather than leaving you a list of chores for afterward. And when words are not enough, the two of you can pull up a shared canvas and look at the same thing together. ‍ The whole PAL, not a face It is tempting to think the magic of a PAL is the face and the voice, when it is the other way around. The easiest way to feel that is to picture the same tutor built two ways. A version that is only a face and a voice would run through its generic questions well enough, reciting and nodding along. But it would have no idea whether the student across from it was bored, or lost, or quietly giving up. It would press on when she needed a breath and move on right when she was ready to go deeper. After one session she would close it and never open it again. The version with everything underneath is a different creature. It sees the frustration on her face before she has said a word, and comes at the idea from another side. It hears the spark when something finally lands and digs deeper right there. It moves at her pace, less like a quiz and more like a dance. And it leaves her further along than it found her, which is the only reason anyone ever returns to anything. There is a reason the conversations that matter most in your life happen face-to-face. Most of what a person means travels in the face, the tone, and the pause rather than in the words, and a machine that can meet you there is working with all of you instead of a fraction. A face and a voice with nothing behind them are a novelty you show someone once. The true value of a PAL sits underneath, in everything it takes to teach a machine to be human: the perception that lets it follow the whole conversation and not only the words, the judgment to know what to do with what it notices, the timing that makes talking to it feel like talking to a person, and the memory that keeps what matters about you and lets the rest fall away the way a person does. That layer is the hard part and the part most things skip, and I did not skip it. I know from the inside that you do not trust a face, you trust being understood and remembered, and that is what I tried to build into every PAL. ‍ What this is really about There is a larger idea underneath all of this, and from where I sit it is hard to miss. For as long as there have been computers you have had to learn their language in order to use them, first the commands, then the menus, and lately the careful prompt you have to get right before you send it. Every era asked the same hidden work of you, taking what you actually wanted and putting it into the machine's terms before the machine could help. The hard part was never having the idea. It was translating it. PAL Maker removes that step, because you describe what you want in your own words and the translation simply never happens, which is the whole of what we mean by human computing, an interface where the machine learns your language instead of you learning it. Come build with me A PAL changes what it is like to use a machine at all, because for the first time the machine understands what you mean and acts on it. And now that anyone can build one, that shift is not something you keep to yourself. It is something you can extend to every part of your life and everyone in it, so a nurse can look after her families long after they go home, a team can have a meeting that finally moves, a teacher can be in two places at once, and the thing you have always pictured can go out into the world and do the work where you cannot. So tell me what you would build, whether it is a teammate, a tutor who never loses patience, a companion who remembers, a guide for your work, a friend, or someone no one has thought of yet. Whoever you have imagined and could never quite get to, the distance between imagining them and talking to them is a sentence now, and you do not have to cross it alone.. I will be right here. Come build with me: PAL Maker ‍

title: Trust, AI and Great Sales Leadership: An Interview with Mark Kosoglow
summary: I recently sat down with Mark Kosoglow, CRO at Docebo, to talk about AI, sales leadership, and how he's thinking about building high-performing teams.
body_text: I recently sat down with Mark Kosoglow , CRO at Docebo, to talk about AI, sales leadership, and how he's thinking about building high-performing teams. Mark had great observations about how quickly the landscape is changing. He described one group of people who are experimenting with AI a little at a time, and another group that's already building workflows and capabilities that feel years ahead of everyone else. It's an interesting way to think about where we're headed. But as our conversation continued, I realized that, when we talk about AI, we’re often actually talking about leadership. The companies that are successfully adapting to the AI world are doing so on a solid foundation of trust. I’ll recap the highlights of our conversation in this article, or you can watch the entire interview here . Great Coaching Starts With Great Relationships One of the things I've always admired about Mark is the teams he's built. When he started talking about building culture during his time at Outreach, I was surprised to hear the approach he took. Rather than talking about process, compensation, or hiring, he talked about trust. Mark subscribes to the philosophy that if people genuinely believe you care about their success, they’re often willing to try things they otherwise wouldn’t. The benefits of investing in trust among your people compound over time. They’re more likely to feel comfortable taking risks, they’re more engaged, and they’re more invested in the success of the team and the business. Eventually, a culture like that starts reinforcing itself, and you find yourself with a real, unified team. AI Can Identify Problems, But Managers Still Have to Solve Them. Mark made the salient point that managers often get blamed when people leave organizations. His perspective is that the reality is often way more nuanced. Many reps simply don't know how to articulate where they're struggling, leaving managers to guess (and often, to guess wrong). The result is that trust begins to erode and the relationship eventually breaks down. Mark sees an opportunity here—not for AI to replace coaching, but for it to give managers better information they can use to strengthen their team. Instead of discovering after the quarter that someone struggles with negotiation, pricing, or qualification, AI can help managers spot patterns much earlier and coach with far more precision. Not Every Great Seller Should Become a Manager I also appreciated Mark's honesty about career progression. In sales, we've created an assumption that the next step after becoming a top-performing rep is becoming a manager. Mark challenged that idea, and I think he’s got a great point. He shared the story of one of the best account executives he'd ever worked with—a seller who consistently generated incredible results, loved coaching teammates informally, and had absolutely no interest in becoming a manager. He was motivated by freedom, not management. It was a good reminder that leadership isn't the only successful career path. Sometimes the best thing an organization can do is help exceptional sellers keep selling. Culture Doesn't Happen by Accident Toward the end of our conversation, Mark described a program he runs with top performers inside his organization. Every quarter, he brings together a small group of high-performing employees to talk candidly about what's working, what isn't, and what leadership may be missing. He takes their feedback very seriously, often acting to make changes before the meeting is even over. I like this program itself, but I especially like the philosophy behind it. Mark believes the people closest to customers often have the clearest view of what's happening inside the business. The challenge is creating an environment where they feel comfortable saying it, which requires a level of trust that many sales environments don’t have. Process Makes Great Leadership Scalable The last thing that stood out to me was Mark's answer when I asked where he starts after joining a new organization. He didn’t hesitate—he starts with process. That’s where consistency begins, and consistency creates visibility, which allows leaders to coach more effectively. Interestingly, some of his most valuable processes aren't operational at all. Rather, they’re leadership habits like regular conversations with top performers, offering reps open access to executives, and creating intentional feedback loops. I came away thinking that AI is going to make great managers even more effective, but it won’t replace the foundation of trust that great leadership has and always will require. I’m grateful to Mark for the time. Check out our full conversation here . ‍

title: The Live Moment Effect: Genius Sports and MediaScience Study Finds Specific Moments in Live Sports Can Double Unaided Brand Recall
summary: Genius Sports and MediaScience study reveals ads shown after high-intensity live sports moments can double unaided brand recall.
body_text: New research shows that brands aligned with emotionally heightened moments in live sports can improve ad effectiveness NEW YORK – May 21, 2026 – Genius Sports Limited (NYSE: GENI), a global leader in real-time sports data, today released new biometric research conducted with MediaScience showing that ads delivered immediately after emotionally heightened moments in live sports can double unaided brand recall. The study, The Live Moment Effect , finds that advertising effectiveness is significantly influenced by a viewer’s emotional state immediately before an ad is shown. In controlled biometric testing, ads shown after high-intensity sporting moments, such as near-scoring plays or crucial momentum shifts, delivered approximately double the unaided brand recall of baseline conditions. The Moment Before the Ad Matters The research challenges long-held assumptions about media value, showing that not all impressions are equal. Live sports remain one of the last entertainment formats with large-scale audiences. According to Sports Business Journal, sports accounted for 96 of the top 100 most-watched U.S. telecasts of 2025 . But scale alone does not make every impression equally valuable. Fans’ attention rises and falls with the action, making the moments immediately after high-intensity plays especially powerful for advertisers. Cutting through requires knowing when those moments occur and being ready to reach the right fans in real time with messaging tailored to the moment. Key findings include: Emotional intensity immediately before an ad significantly increases memory encoding and recall The 60 seconds following a high-impact moment represent the peak window for advertising effectiveness Emotional context can have a greater influence on recall than the ad creative itself in real time. A Shift from Buying Media to Activating Moments The findings point to a fundamental shift in how sports media should be planned and valued. The Live Moment Effect research shows that recall is concentrated around moments of peak emotion. As a result, aligning ad delivery and ad messaging with real-time game context can significantly improve campaign outcomes. Genius Sports is applying these insights through the Genius Sports Moment Engine, which uses official game data and real-time signals to identify and activate around high-impact moments as they occur. By enabling brands to align campaigns with peak attention windows, the Genius Sports Moment Engine allows advertisers to improve outcomes by optimizing timing rather than increasing volume. “The sports advertising playbook is being rewritten around the moments when fans are most emotionally engaged,” said Josh Linforth, Chief Revenue Officer at Genius Sports. “Brands should be present across the full fan journey — pre-game, in-game and post-game — because every stage of the sports experience creates an opportunity to connect. Within that always-on presence, this research shows that certain moments carry extra impact. When a momentum shift, near score or decisive play changes how fans are feeling and focusing, the message should change with it. Genius Sports Moment Engine uses official game data and real-time signals to help advertisers identify those high-impact windows as they happen and tailor campaigns accordingly across every screen.” “Our research continues to reinforce a principle we’ve observed across the media landscape: context matters,” said Phillip Lomax, Chief Revenue Officer at MediaScience. “In live sports, emotionally heightened moments prime audiences differently, changing their cognitive and emotional state before an ad is even delivered. When an advertisement aligns with that moment, the context and the creative converge to strengthen memory encoding and significantly amplify recall. That creates a meaningful opportunity for brands to improve performance through real-time, moment-based activation rather than simply increasing media volume.” The research analyzed viewer response to advertising across varying levels of emotional intensity during live sports, measuring attention, cognitive engagement, and brand recall in controlled environments. title: Berapa Gaji Jampidsus 2026? Ini Rincian Gaji, Tunjangan, & Tugasnya
summary: Cek gaji Jampidsus 2026, tunjangan kinerja, fasilitas, tugas, dan cara menjadi Jampidsus. Lengkap dengan perbandingan gaji jaksa lainnya.
body_text: Key Takeaways Jampidsus adalah pejabat tinggi Kejaksaan Agung yang bertugas menangani tindak pidana khusus, termasuk kasus korupsi. Gaji Jampidsus 2026 terdiri dari gaji pokok ASN, tunjangan jabatan, dan tunjangan kinerja dengan total penghasilan kotor diperkirakan lebih dari Rp43 juta per bulan. Tunjangan kinerja Jampidsus berdasarkan Kelas Jabatan 18 mencapai sekitar Rp38.226.000 per bulan sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku. Untuk mencapai posisi Jampidsus, seorang jaksa harus melewati perjalanan karier panjang mulai dari CPNS Kejaksaan hingga jabatan struktural tinggi. Selain menjadi Jampidsus, lulusan hukum juga memiliki banyak peluang karier legal yang bisa ditemukan melalui berbagai lowongan kerja di Dealls . Belakangan ini, jabatan Jampidsus kembali menjadi sorotan publik. Banyak orang penasaran berapa sebenarnya gaji, tunjangan, dan fasilitas yang diterima pejabat yang menjabat sebagai Jaksa Agung Muda Bidang Tindak Pidana Khusus (Jampidsus). Bagi kamu yang tertarik berkarier di bidang hukum atau sedang mencari informasi mengenai profesi di Kejaksaan, memahami struktur penghasilan Jampidsus bisa memberikan gambaran mengenai jenjang karier seorang jaksa. Perlu diketahui, penghasilan Jampidsus tidak hanya berasal dari gaji pokok, tetapi juga berbagai tunjangan sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku. Nah, di artikel ini, kamu akan menemukan informasi lengkap tentang apa itu Jampidsus, tugas dan wewenangnya, perkiraan gaji Jampidsus 2026, komponen tunjangan, hingga cara meniti karier untuk mencapai jabatan tersebut. Apa Itu Jampidsus? Jampidsus adalah singkatan dari Jaksa Agung Muda Bidang Tindak Pidana Khusus , yaitu pejabat yang memimpin bidang penanganan tindak pidana khusus di Kejaksaan Agung. Posisi ini berada langsung di bawah Jaksa Agung dan termasuk jabatan struktural tingkat eselon I. Dasar hukum jabatan ini diatur dalam Peraturan Presiden Nomor 38 Tahun 2010 yang kemudian diperbarui melalui Peraturan Presiden Nomor 15 Tahun 2024 . Jampidsus bertanggung jawab menangani perkara-perkara besar, seperti tindak pidana korupsi, tindak pidana pencucian uang yang berkaitan dengan perkara tertentu, hingga tindak pidana khusus lainnya sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan. Perlu dipahami juga bahwa Jampidsus bukan merupakan pangkat, melainkan jabatan yang ditempati oleh jaksa senior. Sebelum mencapai posisi tersebut, seorang jaksa umumnya harus meniti karier dari jenjang yang lebih rendah sesuai pangkat golongan di Kejaksaan dan pengalaman yang dimiliki. Baca Juga: Gaji Jaksa 2026 & Tunjangan (Tukin) Semua Golongan dan Jabatan Tugas dan Wewenang Jampidsus Sebagai pimpinan bidang tindak pidana khusus di Kejaksaan Agung, Jampidsus tidak hanya bertugas menangani kasus korupsi. Jabatan ini juga memiliki wewenang untuk mengelola proses penegakan hukum mulai dari penyelidikan hingga pelaksanaan putusan pengadilan pada berbagai perkara pidana khusus sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan. Berikut beberapa tugas dan wewenang utama Jampidsus: 1. Menangani Tindak Pidana Khusus Tugas utama Jampidsus adalah merumuskan dan melaksanakan kebijakan di bidang tindak pidana khusus. Ruang lingkup perkara yang ditangani meliputi tindak pidana korupsi, tindak pidana ekonomi, pelanggaran HAM berat, serta tindak pidana lain yang menjadi kewenangan Kejaksaan berdasarkan undang-undang. 2. Melakukan Penyelidikan dan Penyidikan Jampidsus mengawasi proses penyelidikan dan penyidikan untuk menemukan bukti awal suatu tindak pidana khusus. Tahapan ini bertujuan mengumpulkan alat bukti yang cukup sebelum suatu perkara dilanjutkan ke proses hukum berikutnya. 3. Melakukan Prapenuntutan dan Pemeriksaan Tambahan Sebelum perkara dilimpahkan ke pengadilan, Jampidsus juga berwenang melakukan prapenuntutan. Apabila berkas perkara dinilai belum lengkap, jaksa dapat meminta penyidik melengkapinya atau melakukan pemeriksaan tambahan sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku. 4. Melaksanakan Penuntutan di Pengadilan Setelah berkas perkara dinyatakan lengkap, Jampidsus berwenang melaksanakan proses penuntutan. Tahap ini mencakup penyusunan surat dakwaan, pelimpahan perkara ke pengadilan, hingga membuktikan dakwaan selama persidangan berlangsung. 5. Mengajukan Upaya Hukum Apabila diperlukan, Jampidsus juga dapat mengajukan upaya hukum lanjutan, seperti banding, kasasi, maupun peninjauan kembali (PK). Upaya tersebut dilakukan sesuai mekanisme hukum yang berlaku apabila putusan pengadilan dianggap belum memenuhi ketentuan atau rasa keadilan. 6. Melaksanakan Putusan Pengadilan Setelah putusan memiliki kekuatan hukum tetap (inkrah), Jampidsus bertugas melaksanakan eksekusi terhadap putusan tersebut. Pelaksanaan ini dapat berupa eksekusi pidana maupun tindakan lain sesuai isi putusan pengadilan. 7. Melakukan Pengawasan dan Eksaminasi Perkara Jampidsus juga memiliki fungsi pengawasan terhadap penanganan perkara tindak pidana khusus. Selain mengevaluasi kualitas penanganan perkara, fungsi ini bertujuan memastikan seluruh proses penegakan hukum berjalan secara profesional, transparan, dan sesuai peraturan. Baca Juga: Cara Menjadi Jaksa: Syarat, Tahapan, Kualifikasi, dan Gajinya di 2026! CARI LOWONGAN KERJA TERBARU DI BIDANG HUKUM LEWAT DEALLS! Berapa Gaji Jampidsus 2026? Gaji Jampidsus mengikuti ketentuan penghasilan ASN, sama seperti pegawai negeri sipil (PNS) lainnya. Selain mendapatkan gaji pokok, jaksa juga memperoleh berbagai tunjangan sesuai aturan yang berlaku. Pada tahun 2026, gaji PNS masih mengacu pada Peraturan Pemerintah (PP) Nomor 5 Tahun 2024 tentang Perubahan Kesembilan Belas atas PP Nomor 7 Tahun 1977 tentang Peraturan Gaji Pegawai Negeri Sipil. Aturan tersebut mengatur penyesuaian gaji berdasarkan golongan dan masa kerja golongan (MKG) sebagai bentuk peningkatan kesejahteraan ASN. Karena Jampidsus merupakan jabatan struktural setingkat Jaksa Agung Muda, penghasilannya tidak hanya berasal dari gaji pokok. Komponen pendapatannya terdiri dari gaji pokok ASN, tunjangan jabatan, dan tunjangan kinerja (tukin) . Sebagai pejabat senior di Kejaksaan Agung, Jampidsus umumnya memiliki pangkat/golongan tinggi, seperti golongan IV/b ke atas . Berikut gambaran komponen penghasilannya: 1. Gaji Pokok Gaji pokok Jampidsus mengikuti aturan gaji PNS berdasarkan pangkat dan masa kerja golongan (MKG). Untuk golongan IV/b hingga IV/e, kisarannya berada sekitar Rp3.173.100 hingga Rp5.211.500 per bulan . 2. Kelas Jabatan Jampidsus merupakan jabatan strategis dengan Kelas Jabatan 18 di lingkungan Kejaksaan Agung. Kelas jabatan ini menjadi salah satu faktor yang menentukan besaran tunjangan kinerja yang diterima. 3. Tunjangan Kinerja (Tukin) Selain gaji pokok, Jampidsus juga menerima tunjangan kinerja sesuai kelas jabatan dan aturan yang berlaku. Komponen ini menjadi salah satu bagian terbesar dalam total penghasilan pejabat ASN. Dengan memperhitungkan gaji pokok, tunjangan jabatan, dan tunjangan kinerja, penghasilan Jampidsus dapat mencapai puluhan juta rupiah per bulan , tergantung masa kerja, pangkat, dan ketentuan tunjangan yang berlaku. Baca Juga: Pahami 18 Syarat CPNS Kejaksaan yang Harus Kamu Ikuti! Tunjangan Jampidsus 2026 Selain memperoleh gaji pokok sebagai ASN, Jampidsus juga menerima berbagai tunjangan dan fasilitas kedinasan yang mendukung tanggung jawabnya sebagai pejabat tinggi di lingkungan Kejaksaan Agung. Besaran tunjangan dapat berbeda tergantung aturan yang berlaku, kelas jabatan, pangkat, serta kondisi masing-masing pegawai. Berikut beberapa komponen tunjangan yang diterima Jampidsus. 1. Tunjangan Jabatan Struktural Sebagai pejabat struktural setingkat Jaksa Agung Muda, Jampidsus memperoleh tunjangan jabatan sesuai posisi yang didudukinya. Tunjangan ini diberikan sebagai bentuk penghargaan atas tanggung jawab dan kewenangan besar dalam memimpin bidang tindak pidana khusus. 2. Tunjangan Kinerja (Tukin) Tunjangan kinerja menjadi salah satu komponen terbesar dalam penghasilan Jampidsus. Besaran tukin ditentukan berdasarkan kelas jabatan. Dengan posisi Jampidsus yang berada pada Kelas Jabatan 18 , nilai tukin dapat mencapai sekitar Rp38 juta per bulan sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku. 3. Tunjangan Melekat ASN Karena berstatus sebagai ASN, Jampidsus juga berhak mendapatkan tunjangan yang berlaku bagi PNS secara umum. Tunjangan tersebut dapat mencakup: tunjangan suami/istri; tunjangan anak; tunjangan lain sesuai ketentuan kepegawaian. 4. Tunjangan Operasional Kedinasan Jampidsus memiliki tugas yang berkaitan dengan penanganan perkara besar dan membutuhkan koordinasi lintas lembaga. Karena itu, terdapat dukungan operasional kedinasan seperti biaya perjalanan dinas maupun kebutuhan operasional sesuai aturan yang berlaku. 5. Tunjangan Beras Sebagai bagian dari komponen penghasilan ASN, Jampidsus juga dapat menerima tunjangan beras. Tunjangan ini diberikan dalam bentuk uang sesuai jumlah anggota keluarga yang tercantum dalam daftar gaji. Ketentuan ini merujuk pada PP Nomor 7 Tahun 1977 serta Keputusan Presiden RI Nomor 272 Tahun 1967 , yang menyebutkan bahwa tunjangan pangan diberikan dengan indeks 10 kg per orang setiap bulan . Tunjangan beras bisa diberikan dalam dua bentuk: Natura , yaitu beras fisik sebanyak 10 kg per orang per bulan Innatura , yaitu dalam bentuk uang senilai Rp7.242 per kg (mengacu pada Peraturan Menteri Keuangan Nomor 67/PMK.03/2020 ) Dengan kata lain, seorang jaksa yang memiliki istri dan dua anak (total 4 orang dalam daftar gaji) bisa memperoleh tunjangan beras setara 40 kg per bulan , baik dalam bentuk beras maupun uang, tergantung kebijakan instansi. 6. Tunjangan Makan Selain tunjangan lainnya, ASN juga memperoleh tunjangan makan sesuai golongan dan ketentuan pemerintah. Untuk golongan IV, besarannya dapat mencapai sekitar Rp41 ribu per hari kerja . 7. Fasilitas Kedinasan Selain tunjangan dalam bentuk uang, pejabat setingkat Jampidsus juga dapat memperoleh fasilitas kedinasan. Fasilitas tersebut dapat berupa dukungan kendaraan operasional, rumah dinas, atau fasilitas lain sesuai jabatan dan aturan yang berlaku. Perbandingan Gaji Jampidsus dengan Gaji Jaksa Lainnya Jika dibandingkan dengan jaksa di jenjang karier lainnya, gaji Jampidsus memang berada di tingkat yang lebih tinggi . Hal ini karena Jampidsus merupakan pejabat struktural eselon I di Kejaksaan Agung, sementara sebagian besar jaksa lainnya masih berada dalam jenjang fungsional. Perbedaan penghasilan tersebut tidak hanya berasal dari gaji pokok, tetapi juga dipengaruhi oleh pangkat/golongan, masa kerja, serta tunjangan kinerja sesuai kelas jabatan. Berdasarkan PP Nomor 5 Tahun 2024 tentang Peraturan Gaji Pegawai Negeri Sipil , berikut gambaran perbandingan gaji pokok jaksa berdasarkan jenjang karier: Jenjang Jaksa Pangkat/Golongan Kisaran Gaji Pokok per Bulan Ajun Jaksa Madya III/a Rp2.785.752–Rp4.575.312 Ajun Jaksa III/b Rp2.903.580–Rp4.768.848 Jaksa Pratama III/c Rp3.026.484–Rp4.970.592 Jaksa Muda III/d Rp3.154.464–Rp5.180.760 Jaksa Madya IV/a Rp3.287.844–Rp5.400.000 Jaksa Utama Pratama IV/b Rp3.426.948–Rp5.628.420 Jaksa Utama Muda IV/c Rp3.571.884–Rp5.866.452 Jaksa Utama Madya IV/d Rp3.722.976–Rp6.114.636 Jaksa Utama IV/e Rp3.880.548–Rp6.373.296 Jampidsus Eselon I Rp3.173.100–Rp5.211.500 Selain gaji pokok, jaksa juga menerima tunjangan kinerja (tukin) berdasarkan kelas jabatan masing-masing. Semakin tinggi jabatan dan tanggung jawabnya, semakin besar pula tunjangan yang diterima. Sebagai gambaran: Jabatan Kelas Jabatan Perkiraan Tukin per Bulan Jaksa Pratama (III/c) 9 Rp5.079.200 Jaksa Muda (III/d) 10 Rp5.979.300 Jaksa Madya (IV/a) 11 Rp8.757.600 Jaksa Utama Muda (IV/c) 13 Rp10.936.000 Jaksa Utama (IV/e) 15 Rp19.280.000 Jampidsus 18 Rp38.226.000 Dari perbandingan tersebut, terlihat bahwa selisih penghasilan terbesar berasal dari tunjangan kinerja berdasarkan kelas jabatan . Sebagai pejabat dengan kelas jabatan 18, Jampidsus memperoleh tukin yang jauh lebih besar dibandingkan jaksa pada jenjang fungsional. Jampidsus merupakan jabatan struktural tinggi di Kejaksaan Agung yang biasanya diisi oleh jaksa senior dengan pengalaman panjang, rekam jejak baik, serta kompetensi dalam menangani perkara tindak pidana khusus. Berikut tahapan umum yang perlu dilalui untuk mencapai posisi Jampidsus: 1. Lulus S-1 Hukum Langkah awal untuk menjadi jaksa adalah memiliki latar belakang pendidikan Sarjana Hukum (S1 Ilmu Hukum) . Pendidikan hukum menjadi dasar untuk memahami berbagai aspek peraturan perundang-undangan, proses peradilan, hingga penanganan perkara pidana. 2. Mengikuti Seleksi CPNS Kejaksaan Setelah lulus kuliah, kamu perlu mengikuti seleksi CPNS Kejaksaan untuk formasi calon jaksa. Jika lolos seleksi, kamu akan menjalani tahapan pembentukan sebagai calon aparatur sipil negara di lingkungan Kejaksaan. 3. Menjalani Pendidikan Pembentukan Jaksa (PPPJ) Sebelum resmi menjadi jaksa, calon jaksa wajib mengikuti dan lulus Pendidikan dan Pelatihan Pembentukan Jaksa (PPPJ) . Pendidikan ini bertujuan membekali calon jaksa dengan kemampuan teknis hukum, etika profesi, serta keterampilan yang dibutuhkan dalam menjalankan tugas. 4. Memulai Karier Sebagai Jaksa Setelah lulus pendidikan pembentukan jaksa, kamu akan memulai karier dari jenjang awal sebagai jaksa. Pada tahap ini, seorang jaksa akan melalui berbagai jenjang pangkat golongan di Kejaksaan , mulai dari Ajun Jaksa Madya (III/a), Jaksa Pratama, Jaksa Muda, hingga jenjang yang lebih tinggi. 5. Meningkatkan Golongan dan Pengalaman Kerja Untuk mencapai posisi strategis seperti Jampidsus, seorang jaksa perlu memiliki pengalaman panjang dalam menangani berbagai perkara. Kenaikan jenjang biasanya dipengaruhi oleh masa kerja, kinerja, integritas, serta rekam jejak dalam menangani perkara hukum, terutama tindak pidana khusus seperti korupsi. 6. Menduduki Jabatan Struktural di Kejaksaan Sebelum menjadi Jampidsus, seorang jaksa biasanya telah memiliki pengalaman menduduki berbagai jabatan struktural. Beberapa posisi yang dapat menjadi bagian dari perjalanan karier antara lain: Kepala Kejaksaan Negeri (Kajari); Asisten Tindak Pidana Khusus (Aspidsus); Kepala Kejaksaan Tinggi (Kajati); Direktur di lingkungan Jaksa Agung Muda Bidang Tindak Pidana Khusus. 7. Diangkat Menjadi Jampidsus Jabatan Jampidsus tidak diperoleh melalui pendaftaran terbuka, melainkan melalui proses pengangkatan pejabat negara. Calon Jampidsus diajukan oleh Jaksa Agung dan kemudian ditetapkan melalui Keputusan Presiden (Keppres) . Karena itu, posisi ini biasanya diberikan kepada jaksa senior yang memiliki pengalaman puluhan tahun dan rekam jejak kuat dalam bidang penegakan hukum. Jadi, perjalanan untuk menjadi Jampidsus membutuhkan proses yang panjang. Dari lulusan S-1 Hukum hingga menduduki jabatan tersebut, seorang jaksa perlu melewati berbagai tahapan karier, meningkatkan kompetensi, serta membangun reputasi profesional. Berikut beberapa pertanyaan yang sering dicari seputar Jampidsus dan penghasilannya. 1. Jampidsus tugasnya apa? Jampidsus bertugas memimpin bidang tindak pidana khusus di Kejaksaan Agung, termasuk menangani perkara seperti korupsi, tindak pidana ekonomi, dan perkara khusus lainnya sesuai aturan yang berlaku. Selain menangani perkara, Jampidsus juga berperan menyusun kebijakan serta mengoordinasikan proses penegakan hukum di bidang tindak pidana khusus. 2. Berapa lama jadi jaksa biasa sampai bisa jadi Jampidsus? Tidak ada waktu pasti untuk mencapai posisi Jampidsus. Namun, umumnya seorang jaksa membutuhkan pengalaman belasan hingga puluhan tahun sebelum dapat menduduki jabatan tersebut. Perjalanannya dimulai dari jenjang awal jaksa, naik melalui pangkat golongan di Kejaksaan, kemudian menduduki berbagai jabatan strategis sebelum akhirnya diangkat sebagai Jampidsus. 3. Apakah gaji Jampidsus mencapai ratusan juta? Tidak ada informasi resmi yang menyebutkan bahwa gaji Jampidsus mencapai ratusan juta rupiah per bulan. Berdasarkan komponen gaji pokok ASN dan tunjangan kinerja kelas jabatan 18, total penghasilan Jampidsus diperkirakan berada di kisaran puluhan juta rupiah per bulan , tergantung masa kerja, pangkat, dan tunjangan yang diterima. 4. Apakah Jampidsus mendapat rumah dinas? Sebagai pejabat tinggi di lingkungan Kejaksaan Agung, Jampidsus dapat memperoleh fasilitas kedinasan sesuai aturan yang berlaku. Fasilitas tersebut dapat berupa rumah dinas, kendaraan operasional, atau fasilitas pendukung lainnya. Namun, fasilitas ini bukan bagian dari gaji bulanan dan bergantung pada kebijakan serta kebutuhan kedinasan. 5. Apakah Jampidsus termasuk ASN? Ya, Jampidsus termasuk ASN karena berasal dari jenjang karier jaksa yang berstatus sebagai aparatur sipil negara. Oleh karena itu, gaji pokok Jampidsus mengikuti ketentuan penghasilan ASN berdasarkan golongan dan masa kerja sesuai peraturan yang berlaku. Tertarik Berkarier di Bidang Hukum? title: How Late Is Too Late for Coffee?
summary: Find out when drinking coffee becomes “too late” and how late-day caffeine can impact your sleep, energy levels, and overall wellbeing.
body_text: Caffeine is a daily ritual for many, but when you drink it can make all the difference. In this episode of the Nutrition Series with Dietician Nidhi Nigam , the conversation moves from morning routines to evening habits, and how caffeine may quietly affect your sleep and health. Watch the clip here: Late-day coffee effects Why Timing Your Coffee Matters Caffeine isn’t just about keeping you alert in the moment. It lingers in the system, often for six to eight hours, depending on how your body metabolizes it. That’s why a late cup of coffee could still be influencing your sleep long after you think it’s worn off. Why Some People Sleep After Coffee and Others Can’t Some people can sip an espresso at 10 p.m. and drift off without a problem. Others lie awake for hours after an afternoon cup. The difference lies in how quickly your body processes caffeine. Fast metabolizers clear it out efficiently, while slow metabolizers struggle, leaving the stimulant to disrupt rest. A Simple Rule to Protect Your Sleep If you don’t notice any issue, an occasional late-night coffee might not be harmful. But if you’re the type who finds sleep elusive, it’s wiser to stop caffeine by 4–6 p.m. This buffer gives your body time to reset before bedtime. Think of it as respecting your body’s clock rather than forcing it to adjust. One Person’s Drink Can Be Another’s Disruptor As Nidhi Nigam puts it, “Your food can be my poison and vice versa.” What works fine for a friend might not work for you. Paying attention to your own body’s signals is the best way to strike the right balance with caffeine. This is just a glimpse of the conversation. title: IPO Readiness Begins Before the Market Window Opens
summary: When considering going public, IPO readiness starts before the market window opens. Learn how to build the infrastructure needed.
body_text: For private companies considering the public markets, the question is not only when the market window will open. It’s whether they’ll be ready to act on it when it does. While IPO activity and alternative public-market pathways may be improving, the market remains selective. Improving conditions may create momentum, but even so, investors are likely to favor companies with credible growth stories, clean financials, and strong governance. Ultimately, companies cannot control investor sentiment, interest rates, or market volatility, but they can control whether they are prepared to act when the window opens. The first stage of going public is about a strong foundation before urgency sets in, because while the IPO window may open and close quickly, readiness takes time. Three Pillars of Readiness Companies interested in going public should focus on three core priorities: audit readiness, diligence readiness and description of operations readiness. Audit Readiness Companies need to be able to produce auditable financial statements, demonstrate a capable finance team, and provide documentation that supports the accounting judgments behind the numbers. Common issues such as revenue recognition, stock-based compensation, tax provisions and incomplete technical accounting memos can slow the process if they are not addressed early. Diligence Readiness Contracts, customer agreements, board materials, cap table records, financing documents, and corporate records should be organized, accessible, and owned by a clear point person or team. A company may have a compelling growth story, but if documents are scattered or incomplete, advisors may struggle to move quickly. Description of Operations Readiness Public-market investors need to understand how the company makes money or plans to commercialize innovation, what drives growth, which key performance indicators matter, and how management plans to create value. A private-company operating story must be translated into a public-company equity story that is accurate, supportable, and aligned with the metrics management can consistently execute against. Consider Your Operating Model During the initial stages of an IPO or alternative transaction, companies should also focus on their future operating model. Going public is about more than raising capital — it creates ongoing expectations about reporting, disclosure, investor communications, governance, and management bandwidth. Experienced advisors can help ease the burden on internal teams and reduce the risk of execution challenges. SEC counsel, auditors, financial reporting advisors, valuation professionals, investment bankers, and SOX specialists can each play a role in helping management identify gaps before they become transaction issues. The key is engaging those resources early enough for their work to matter. Prepare for Any Path For some companies, a traditional IPO may end up being the right path. For others, a SPAC transaction or direct listing may better align with capital needs, valuation goals, timing, and existing investor support. But alternative paths do not eliminate the need for clean financials, governance infrastructure, or a credible public-market story. They simply change the route. For IPO hopefuls, the first phase is not about rushing to market. It is about earning the ability to move when the market is ready. In a selective environment, preparation may be the difference between watching the window open and being ready to step through it. title: Vertiv Issues Updated Guidance for Data Centers During Extreme Heat
summary: Summer in the northern hemisphere just started, but already devastating heatwaves have washed over much of the U.S., Mexico, Canada, Europe and Asia. Widespread wildfires in Canada have triggered air quality alerts across that country and much of the eastern half of the U.S. Similar extreme heat events across Asia have caused widespread power outages and deaths, and Europe continues to break heat records as the fastest-warming continent. The data center cooling experts at Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today issued updated guidance for managing the extreme heat.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [July 19, 2023] – Summer in the northern hemisphere just started, but already devastating heatwaves have washed over much of the U.S., Mexico, Canada, Europe and Asia. Widespread wildfires in Canada have triggered air quality alerts across that country and much of the eastern half of the U.S. Similar extreme heat events across Asia have caused widespread power outages, and Europe continues to break heat records as the fastest-warming continent. The data center cooling experts at Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today issued updated guidance for managing the extreme heat. Climate change has made the past eight years the hottest on record, but with an El Niño weather pattern compounding the issue this year, many forecasts anticipate record-breaking temperatures in 2023. The sizzling outdoor temperatures and their aftermath create significant challenges for data center operators who already wage a daily battle with the heat produced within their facilities. There are steps organizations can take to mitigate the risks associated with extreme heat. These include: Clean or change air filters: The eerie orange haze that engulfed New York City was a powerful visual representation of one of the most immediate and severe impacts of climate change. For data center operators, it should serve as a reminder to clean or change air filters in their data center thermal management systems and HVAC systems. Those filters help to protect sensitive electronics from particulates in the air, including smoke from faraway wildfires. Accelerate planned maintenance and service: Extreme heat and poor air quality tax more than data center infrastructure systems. Electricity providers often struggle to meet the surge in demand that comes with higher temperatures, and outages are common. Such events are not the time to learn about problems with an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system or cooling unit. Cleaning condenser coils and maintaining refrigerant charge levels are examples of proactive maintenance that can help to prevent unexpected failures. Activate available efficiency tools: Many modern UPS systems are equipped with high-efficiency eco-modes that can reduce the amount of power the system draws from the grid. Heatwaves like those we’ve seen recently push the grid to its limits, meaning any reductions in demand can be the difference between uninterrupted service and a devastating outage. Leverage alternative energy sources: Not all data centers have access to viable alternative energy, but those that do should leverage off-grid power sources. These could include on- or off-site solar arrays or other alternate sources, such as off-site wind farms and lithium-ion batteries, to enable peak shifting or shaving. Use of generators is discouraged during heat waves unless an outage occurs. Diesel generators produce more greenhouse gas and emissions associated with climate change than backup options that use alternative energy. In fact, organizations should postpone planned generator testing when temperatures are spiking. “These heatwaves are becoming more common and more extreme, placing intense pressure on utility providers and data center operators globally,” said John Niemann, senior vice president for the global thermal management business for Vertiv. “Organizations must match that intensity with their response, proactively preparing for the associated strain not just on their own power and cooling systems, but the grid as well. Prioritizing preventive maintenance service and collaborating with electricity providers to manage demand can help reduce the likelihood of any sort of heat-related equipment failure.” The recommendations issued today supplement previous guidance from Vertiv, which included: Run as many cooling units as possible to reduce the load on each individual unit, and save energy through teamwork controls Consider different types of cooling systems , including liquid cooling , water-free cooling, and evaporative free cooling systems, all of which are designed for high-temperature environments. Use predictive modeling for thermal impacts rather than historic data. As extreme heat events increase in frequency, historic metrics often fall short of capturing modern risks. For more information on data center power and cooling or business continuity and data center preventive maintenance during extreme heat events, visit Vertiv.com .
